title: Great, Green Gobs of Greasy, Grimy Gopher Guts or Green Goddess Kugel
description:
Name adapted from Food & Wine for our 2026 PSU vs Minnesota Golden Gophers tailgate with Keith, Kent & Paul, among others – “The Galls & The Gangs Grill the Golden Gophers.”
A trio of fresh herbs, plenty of lemon zest, and creamy farmer cheese give this savory noodle kugel its vivid green hue and lively flavor.
ingredients: 2 (5-ounce) bunches scallions, cut into 1-inch-long pieces (about 4 cups)
1 cup packed fresh dill, large stems removed (about 1 ounce)
1 cup packed fresh parsley, large stems removed (about 1 ounce)
12 ounces wide egg noodles (or spaghetti for guts) (about 6 1/2 cups)
1/4 cup unsalted butter, cut into 1-tablespoon pieces
15 ounces farmer cheese or whole-milk ricotta cheese
directions: Preheat oven to 375°F. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over medium-high. Prepare a large bowl of ice water, and place beside stovetop.

Add scallions, chives, dill, and parsley to boiling water, using tongs to ensure herbs are fully submerged; boil until bright green and tender, about 1 minute. Remove herbs, using tongs and a fine wire-mesh strainer as needed, and transfer to prepared ice water; let cool for 1 minute. Remove herbs from ice water, and place on paper towels; squeeze out as much liquid as possible. Place herbs in a food processor, and set aside.

Return salted water to a boil over medium-high. Add egg noodles; cook according to package directions. Drain well, and place in a large bowl. Add butter, and toss until noodles are well coated. Set aside until ready to use.

Add cheese, oil, lemon zest, salt, pepper, and garlic to food processor with herbs; process until herbs are coarsely chopped and mixture resembles pesto, 1 to 2 minutes, stopping to scrape down sides as needed. Add egg, and process until just combined, about 10 seconds. Add sauce to the cooked noodles, stirring until well coated.
Transfer noodle mixture to a 2-quart baking dish, smoothing top into an even layer. Bake until kugel is beginning to brown on top, 25 to 28 minutes. Serve hot.
